{{Quote|I must say, he looks like a thoroughly nasty fellow.''"<br />"''He is.|[[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]|<ref name="SW68">[[Star Wars (1977) 68|''Star Wars'' (1977) 68]]</ref>}}
'''Dengar''', also known as "'''Payback'''," was a [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] and the pilot of the [[Punishing One/Legends|''Punishing One'']]. Brought up in the culture of [[Swoop/Legends|swoop bikes]] and becoming a successful racer himself, Dengar also led a double life as a successful [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], becoming one of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] most efficient [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]]; his [[Safe cargo objective/Legends|work]] teamed him with the likes of bounty hunters such as [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] and [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]]. Dengar would eventually give up the life of bounty hunting to pursue his other passion: [[Swoop racing/Legends|swoop racing]].

Following a grievous injury sustained at the hands of the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] during a swoop race through [[Agrilat Region|Agrilat]] Swamp on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], Dengar was rebuilt by the scientists of the Galactic Empire as an [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]], augmented by various neuro-implants and cybernetic enhancements and being void of all emotions besides rage, despair, and hope. Dengar served under the Empire until he refused to kill the [[Holy Children of Asrat]]; sensing the despair in the children, Dengar deserted his post and became a freelance gun-for hire. It was after a bounty was posted on Han Solo by the Empire that he became entangled in the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], serving under the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] in [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] with the intention of taking Solo when he had the chance. Due to a chance encounter, Dengar was among an elite group of hunters recruited by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] to capture Solo and the passengers of the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] shortly after the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|Thought you could run from me, hey Solo?|Dengar|<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar">{{StoryCite|story=Payback: The Tale of Dengar|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref>}}
===Early life===
[[File:Dengar-FFp57.png|thumb|left|Dengar during the Clone Wars]]
Dengar was born on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] and as a young child, he worked with his father repairing and tuning [[Swoop/Legends|swoops]]. This early experience lead to him becoming a well-known and successful [[Swoop/Legends|swoop]] racer for the [[Ferini team]] during his youth.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" /> By the time he reached pre-adolescence, he was considered something of a cult hero throughout the [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian system]]. Through his connections with the Ferini team, he gained endorsements and higher wages and winnings.

===Bounty hunter===
By [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], Dengar had established himself as a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], keeping a respectable track record. He eventually became a member of a posse of hunters consisting of [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]], [[Latts Razzi/Legends|Latts Razzi]], [[C-21 Highsinger/Legends|C-21 Highsinger]], and [[Oked/Legends|Oked]]. Dengar and company were hired to escort a [[Hovertrain/Legends|hovertrain]] containing cargo valuable to [[Otua Blank/Legends|Otua Blank]], the leader of the [[Belugan/Legends|Belugan]] people of [[Quarzite/Legends|Quarzite]]. Dengar and company prepared for the mission on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], making a last minute addition to the team: [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]], a (unbeknownst to them) [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] who [[Death/Legends|killed]] Oked in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]].<ref name="CW4.20">{{TCW|Bounty (episode)}}</ref>

Dengar and company set off in the [[Hound's Tooth/Legends|''Hound's Tooth'']] to Quarzite, where Major [[Rigosso/Legends|Rigosso]] transported the team to the train's subterranean loading dock via a [[space elevator]] from an orbital [[Skyhook/Legends|skyhook]]. Dengar, along with Ventress, were assigned to guard the rear of the train. After unsuccessfully flirting with Ventress, a team of skilled [[Kage Warriors/Legends|Kage Warriors]] boarded the train in an attempt to retrieve the cargo. Dengar managed to fight off many of the attackers due to his skilled hand-to-hand combat techniques, and even managed to kill two using sticky explosives. Dengar was eventually overwhelmed by the attackers and was thrown from the train, landing safely on the subterranean surface. Dengar and his allies, who were likewise thrown from the train, returned to the skyhook to await Ventress, who had betrayed the mission objective by swapping the cargo with Boba Fett, who was bound and gagged.<ref name="CW4.20" />

Dengar was employed soon by the Hutts alongside Latts, [[Embo/Legends|Embo]], and [[Sugi (bounty hunter)/Legends|Sugi]] as protection on [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]]. They were present when [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]], and [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] leader, [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]] came to ally with the Hutts. When the plan went sour, the four bounty hunters attacked, though they were pushed by the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian's]] flamethrower. The trio soon received reinforcements and attacked. When the battle was clearly lost, Dengar and Latts saved the beaten Embo and Sugi by covering their escape with smoke grenades. The group of mercenaries fled the Death Watch and their [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] allies.

===The swoop accident===
At some point prior to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Dengar, having mastered the professional swoop circuit on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], was called to the private tour, where more dangerous challenges awaited him.<ref name="EGC" /><ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" /> He was constantly compared to a young swoop jockey on the private circuit named [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]. Eager to prove his superiority, Dengar challenged Solo to a winner-takes-all [[Swoop racing/Legends|race]] through the [[Crystal/Legends|crystal]] swamps of [[Agrilat Region|Agrilat]]. On the final stretch of the race, Solo brought his swoop down directly over and in front of Dengar, burning his face in the swoop's exhaust and locking the [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsor]] fins of both swoops. The maneuver sent Dengar flying off of his swoop to crash headfirst into crystalline [[Plant/Legends|plants]]. One crystalline stem directly impaled his [[Brain/Legends|brain]], leaving him in a condition so perilous that only the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire's]] doctors had the ability to repair him to a near-natural state. Dengar was kicked out of professional swoop racing for engaging in the illegal race and was abandoned by his friends on the Ferini team. Part of the Agrilat Swamp Racing Circuit eventually became known as ''Dengar's End'', in honor of his accident.<ref name="Star Wars Galaxy Magazine">''[[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine]]''</ref> With his life in ruins, Dengar became viciously embittered with Solo, upon whom he vowed his vengeance.<ref name="EGC" /><ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

As it was, to save his life, Dengar was forced to become part [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] through Imperial experimentation. The parts of his brain controlling his senses of compassion, mercy, and pity were removed, leaving him an emotionless killer. He was only left with rage, hope and, accidentally, loneliness, the only emotions the Imperial doctors decided he would need to fulfill his new duties as an [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]]. Particularly, the doctors allowed him to feel hope at the empty promise that if Dengar was successful in serving the Empire, he would be returned to his old self. He was also fitted with a number of cybernetic implants, such as new, more powerfully-enhanced [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and [[Ear/Legends|ears]], and a drug-induced flawless memory, which left him susceptible to hallucinations. His hypothalamus gland was cut out and replaced with a central [[Computer/Legends|computer]] module to control his new systems.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

He briefly worked as a [[Gladiator/Legends|gladiator]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Loovria/Legends|Loovria]],<ref name="EGC" /> before the Empire employed him as an assassin, a task Dengar carried out ruthlessly and without question until after he was ordered to kill the [[Holy Children of Asrat]]. These children denounced the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] and declared their official desire to leave the Empire. Faced with killing children or deserting the Empire, Dengar chose to leave. Despite no longer being able to feel the difference between good and evil, he still recognized the disparity when he saw it. The Empire posted a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] for his desertion.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

===Return to bounty hunting===
====Lethal assassin====
{{Quote|You can imagine that someone as famous as me gets more bounties than he can accept.|Dengar|<ref name="Agents of Deception">{{SWGTCG|set=Agents of Deception|scenario=Punish the Pirates promotional scenario}}</ref>}}
[[File:Dengar_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Dengar on the hunt]]
Sometime after his desertion from Imperial service, Dengar became a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] again after learning of a price on Han Solo's head. Drawing from his vast Imperial assassin experience, he quickly came into the service of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] despite a debatable record at best. Of the twenty-three bounties he'd collected, only six were taken alive.<ref name="EGC" /> During the Galactic Civil War, he encountered Solo a number of times. Once, just before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], while searching for the [[Yavin Vassilika]],<ref name="Star Wars: Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika">''[[Star Wars: Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika]]''</ref> and then twice in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] before the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]: once on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], when Solo attempted to reunite Jabba the Hutt with his nephew [[Grubba Desilijic Aarrpo|Grubba]],<ref name="Star Wars Missions 6: The Search for Grubba the Hutt">''[[Star Wars Missions 6: The Search for Grubba the Hutt]]''</ref> and then again while teamed up with [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], [[Skorr/Legends|Skorr]], and [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]] in a showdown with Solo, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], and the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Raskar]] on [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]].<ref name="The Bounty Hunter of Ord Mantell">"[[The Bounty Hunter of Ord Mantell]]"</ref> Still, Dengar was never able to capture Solo; it seemed as if Solo always got the best of him and was always one step ahead of him. Dengar often remarked to himself that all he ever saw of Solo was the aft of the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] as it was flying away from him.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

His career as a bounty hunter and assassin even saw him targeting Imperials, specifically officers of [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|COMPNOR's]] Redesign efforts. Dengar believed that COMPNOR was the most evil branch of the Empire. This included COMPNOR [[General/Legends|General]] [[Sinick Kritkeen]] on the planet [[Aruza/Legends|Aruza]]. During this mission, the [[Aruzan/Legends|Aruzans]] paid him a small bounty to assassinate Kritkeen in the hopes that the Empire would abandon their Redesign efforts of Aruza. There, Dengar saved an Aruzan woman named [[Manaroo/Legends|Manaroo]], who would soon become an integral part of his life.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" /> At some point, he also contacted a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] to deliver a "message" to pirate captain [[Nym/Legends|Nym]] on [[Lok/Legends|Lok]].<ref name="Agents of Deception" />

[[File:Dengar_on_Nal_Hutta_SWITESB.jpg|thumb|left|Dengar on Nal Hutta]]
Following the [[battle of Talus]], Dengar was one of many bounty hunters involved in capturing [[Emperor's Most Wanted]], individuals from a list of high-paid bounties on critical [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] leaders. Dengar had scored a big bounty on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], and then traveled to [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] to hand it over to the Empire. From [[Moenia/Legends|Moenia]], he made his way to the Imperial outpost at [[Dee'ja Peak/Legends|Dee'ja Peak]], where he engaged in a conversation with several sneaky-looking individuals. In the midst of the conversation, they were interrupted by an arrival of several individuals in a [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]]. They explained that they worked for [[Borvo]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]], who, reportedly, had a job for Dengar. However, Dengar was suspicious, and the individuals revealed themselves to be in fact Rebel agents looking for the location of the captured Rebel leaders. With uncanny speed, Dengar drew his blasters and started the firefight, his associates joined him immediately. However, while the Corellian bounty hunter put up a strong defense, his companions were all killed, forcing Dengar to surrender. He explained that he handed over the bounty to Imperial authorities at the outpost in Dee'ja Peak, but did not know the location where the prisoners were being held. When pressed, he added that, according to rumors, [[Snoova]] had recently delivered a bounty to the same outpost as well. The Rebels went in pursuit of the trail, while handing Dengar over to the Rebel authorities for questioning.<ref>{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|scenario=Light Side scenario campaign}}</ref> He was later seen walking free on [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]] in [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], seeking bounty hunting work from the Hutts.<ref name="SWITESB">{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Illustrated: The Empire Strikes Back|cardname=One Year Earlier: Dengar}}</ref>

On the planet [[Toola/Legends|Toola]], Dengar was recruited by an unnamed woman to join the Rebel Alliance, who had taken notice of his targeting of Imperial officials. The woman secretly programmed the coordinates for an unnamed [[Star/Legends|star]] on the farthest rim of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] into his [[Starship/Legends|ship's]] [[Navigation computer/Legends|navicomputer]], where he found a hidden Rebel outpost. There, he was examined by military intelligence officers and accepted assignment to a newly-formed outpost on the planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. However, his true intention for joining the Rebellion was that he knew wherever the Rebellion was would be where he would find Han Solo.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

====The hunt for Solo====
[[File:DengarIG88Fett-TESB30.png|thumb|right|250px|Dengar, IG-88B and Boba Fett answered Darth Vader's call for bounty hunters]]
Unfortunately for Dengar, he exited [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] into the [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth system]] in the midst of the Rebel evacuation of the planet. Despite the presence of a [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] and a massive Imperial fleet before him, he recklessly tried to reach the planet's surface in hopes of finding Solo. His ruse of posing as an Imperial [[Scout/Legends|scout]] failed when, riding in the wake of a [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]] of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighters]], Dengar's ship was hit with an ion blast from the planet's surface. Drifting helplessly through space, his ship was [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractored]] in by the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']]. His ship was boarded, Dengar was captured and, the Empire quickly realizing his identity, was imprisoned.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

Aboard the ''Executor'', [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] offered him a reprieve of his death warrant, allowing him the freedom to hunt down Solo and the ''Millennium Falcon''.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" /> Disgusted with the [[Fleet/Legends|fleet's]] inability to capture the fugitive ship, Vader then recruited Dengar and five other bounty hunters to bring him the passengers of the ''Falcon'', possibly believing [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] was one of them. By this time, his bounty hunting record was still unimpressive. He had yet to claim one remarkable bounty.<ref name="Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM">{{StoryCite|story=Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref>

While searching for Solo in the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]], the engines of the [[Punishing One/Legends|''Punishing One'']] were crippled by a [[Bomb/Legends|bomb]] placed by [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], who may have heard of Dengar's death warrant, only to leave Dengar helplessly watching the ''Millennium Falcon'' slowly limp out of the system followed closely by the [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']]. He managed to repair his craft and followed Solo's particle vapor trail to [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin's]] [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]], where he arrived a few days later, again, to see the ''Slave I'' leaving the city with the [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] frozen Han Solo on board. However, it was on Cloud City that Dengar was reunited with Manaroo, where he saved her and several other dancers, for a time, from the Imperial [[Occupation of Bespin|subjugation]] of the city. The woman would soon become a permanent part of his life.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

With Manaroo accompanying him away from Cloud City, the Aruzan woman, pitying Dengar's near-emotionless state, tried to share her own feelings with him through her ''[[Attanni]]'', an Aruzan custom in which two people shared emotions cybernetically. Dengar was able to feel what it was to be [[Human/Legends|Human]] again, feeling what she felt and seeing what she saw. It was from this emotional experience that Dengar was finally able to work with the Rebel Alliance by assisting in the evacuation of the Aruzans from their world, freeing them of their Imperial tormentors. Dengar's primary interest in the matter was to free Manaroo's parents.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

Sometime during [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], a contract had Dengar teaming up with fellow bounty-hunters [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]], [[IG-88B/Legends|IG-88]], [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]], and [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]] on a mission for [[Domina Tagge/Legends|Domina Tagge]] to steal a sacred gem from a temple in the [[Red Nebula/Legends|Red Nebula]].<ref name="Star Wars 50: The Crimson Forever">[[Star Wars (1977) 50|''Star Wars'' (1977) 50]]</ref>

Soon after, Dengar had a run in with [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Princess Leia]] who was searching for information about the location of Solo.<ref name="Princess Leia: Rebel Leader">''[[Princess Leia: Rebel Leader]]''</ref> After an unsuccessful bounty hunt for the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Fenn Shysa]], Dengar was imprisoned and to be handed over to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]]. Promising Leia that he would reveal everything he knew, she distracted Shysa while [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] cut Dengar free. However, Dengar double-crossed the pair, and secretly informed the Empire of Leia's location. The planet was then seized.<ref name="SW68" /> With Dengar's assistance, the Empire overrun the planet of Mandalore. Dengar was however, recaptured by Shysa and Leia, and forced to reveal a possible hideout for Boba Fett and therefore [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]].<ref name="SW69">[[Star Wars (1977) 69|''Star Wars'' (1977) 69]]</ref>

On the planet [[Tertiary Moon of Blimph|Blimph 3]], Dengar and other bounty hunters [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]] and [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]] competed in a bounty for [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] staged by [[Quaffug]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]. Dengar failed in this hunt.<ref name="Scoundel's Wages">''[[The Bounty Hunters: Scoundrel's Wages]]''</ref>

[[File:Dengar.jpg|thumb|left|Dengar, "Payback"]]
Eventually, Dengar and Manaroo traveled to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where he knew Boba Fett would eventually deliver the carbonite frozen Han Solo to [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]]. He soon learned that Solo was indeed alive and being held in [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]]. There, Dengar finally caught up with Solo, clutching the carbonite slab and laughing in the face of his old nemesis. However, in his absence, Manaroo was captured by Jabba's cronies and taken to his palace to work as one of the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord's]] many dancers.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

In a bid to rescue her, Dengar returned to Jabba's Palace, knowing he would have to kill the Hutt to save Manaroo. He witnessed Jabba's ruthlessness when killing Oola, his Twi'lek dancer. Quickly, he formulated a plot with few other members of Jabba's entourage, which Jabba himself soon discovered. The Hutt tasked Boba Fett with personally taking care of Dengar, with the stipulation that he died a painful death by way of the [[The Teeth of Tatooine|Teeth of Tatooine]] in the [[Valley of the Winds]]. The night before Jabba was to execute Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Great Pit of Carkoon]], Fett drugged Dengar and left him at the mercy of Tatooine's elements. Surprisingly, for the second time, Boba Fett had done Dengar a favor, so to speak. Although he left Dengar to die, he allowed him to remain with his armor strapped on, which effectively saved him from the brutally harsh winds until he was saved by Manaroo. Dengar realized that for the second time, Fett refrained from killing him, the first being when he merely disabled the ''Punishing One'' near the Hoth asteroid field instead of destroying it and Dengar outright. Still, he vowed to make Fett pay.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

===Life after 4 ABY===
After being rescued by Manaroo, the two agreed to be [[Marriage/Legends|married]]. Dengar recovered from his wounds after several weeks in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]], racking up enormous medical bills. It was then that he realized that few people were aware that Jabba had died at the Pit of Carkoon. He traveled with Manaroo to the site of the Hutt's death hoping to salvage valuable goods, only to find a badly burned and scarred man on the brink of death, who had apparently killed the [[Sarlacc/Legends|Sarlacc]]. He discovered that this broken man was Boba Fett, having survived from being swallowed by the Sarlacc. With Dengar's newly found compassion, sourced from Manaroo's [[Attanni]] device, he nursed Fett back to health.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" /> Dengar, Fett, and [[Kateel of Kuhlvult]] then survived to a [[Bombing of the Dune Sea|bombing run]] on the Great Pit of Carkoon arranged by [[Kuat (person)|Kuat of Kuat]], the leader of [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]]. This unlikely partnership then led Fett and Dengar on a mission to foil what was believed to be [[Xizor/Legends|Prince Xizor's]] complicated plan to destroy the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]]. To achieve this the pair had to kidnap the powerful Kuat of Kuat.<ref name="The Mandalorian Armor">''[[The Mandalorian Armor]]''</ref> The infamous Fett even served as Dengar's best man during his wedding to Manaroo.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

In [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], Dengar tracked the pirate [[Nosstrick]] to the planet [[Fluwhaka]] for a bounty posted by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. However [[Jodo Kast]], whom Dengar believed to be the feared [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], had arrived first. Dengar entered to see Kast dangling from a spiked pit. Dengar blasted the computer controls to the trapdoor that dropped into the pit, saving Kast's life. Kast responded by pointing a blaster at Dengar and taking the bounty for himself. Realizing that [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] wouldn't have made nearly as many mistakes or threatened to shoot the man that saved his life, Dengar contacted Fett, making him aware of Kast's posturing. Dengar accompanied Fett to [[Paqualis III/Legends|Paqualis III]] where Fett disguised himself as "Sava Brec Madak" and approached the [[House Benelex]] bounty hunters' guild to hire Kast. According to "Madak," a man called Satnik Hiicrop had stolen his name and reputation; Hiicrop, "Madak" said, could be found in a clan keep on [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]], and he wanted Kast to bring him in. Dengar proceeded to help Fett lay traps for Kast in the ruined clan keep, and was present when he was killed.<ref name="Boba Fett: Twin Engines of Destruction">''[[Boba Fett: Twin Engines of Destruction]]''</ref>

Their partnership continued until [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], when the cloned [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor Palpatine]] returned. The pair's final, failed attempts to recapture the elusive Solo on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] and [[Byss/Legends|Byss]] led Dengar to proclaim that he would never work with Fett again.<ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>

===Retirement===
{{Quote|I outwitted him	once, but I wouldn't count on it again. Dengar's one of the best.|Zekk|<ref name="YJK9">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Delusions of Grandeur]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Dengar-NEGTC.png|thumb|right|150px|Dengar]]
After his partnership with Fett, Dengar settled down to married life with Manaroo. However, he resurfaced from time to time for unknown reasons.<ref name="DB" />

In [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] was taken prisoner for a short time by a bounty hunter. She later escaped from him and found an ID card that read "Dengar Roth".<ref name="Dark Force Rising">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref> However, the card was forged and carried by a man named [[Gunner Groth]], who used the phony ID to better scare his targets and negotiate higher bounties with the Empire.<ref name="The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook">''[[The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref>

In [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]] Dengar freelanced for [[Grappa (Hutt)|Grappa]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]], who was paying large sums for bounty hunters. After Grappa's organization began to unravel, Dengar fled, but was captured by the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]], which Grappa had offended. However, after revealing all he knew of Grappa's organization, Black Sun let Dengar go unharmed, and he swore never again to work for a Hutt.<ref name="Handbook 2: Crimson Empire">[[Star Wars Handbook 2: Crimson Empire|''Star Wars Handbook'' 2: ''Crimson Empire'']]</ref>

Over a decade later in [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]], Dengar joined the quest for [[Bornan Thul]] during the [[Diversity Alliance]]'s reign. This brought him face-to-face not only just with an upstart bounty hunter named [[Zekk]], but with [[Darth Caedus|Jacen]] and [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]], the children of his former enemy.<ref name="YJK9" /><ref name="YJK10">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Jedi Bounty]]''</ref> Dengar's ultimate whereabouts and activities remained unknown.<ref name="DB" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Go ahead. Try it. I've got nothing to lose.|Dengar|<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Dengar_Alt_Card_IA_Spring_2016_Tournament_Kit.png|thumb|left|Dengar]]
Early in his life, Dengar was a crude and slovenly bounty hunter with a proven track record, priding himself on firepower and destruction. Though scruffy-looking and battered, he would frequently make passes at women that caught his eye. Despite some perceiving him as obnoxious, a young Boba Fett enjoyed working with him and held him in high regard.

His mind would take a sharp turn following his swoop accident and the bio-implants the Empire used to save his life. Dengar became a person devoid of all caring emotions. His new cybernetics transformed his damaged biological brain into that of an emotionless and remorseless killer. Dengar continually displayed a serious demeanor and would only kill a person professionally, not for amusement. Dengar strongly believed Han Solo was responsible for how he was, and right before any assassination, he would attempt to visualize his target as Han Solo, his need for revenge enhancing his desire to kill.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

During much of his career, he was considered more ruthless than Boba Fett himself, and usually performed assassinations rather than live captures. Nevertheless, traces of self-recrimination and foggy memories of his past plagued his thoughts, resulting in deep self-loathing and despair.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

After he met and married Manaroo, however, his emotions were restored, thanks to the Aruzan Attanni device and Manaroo's will to change him. Following her wishes, Dengar, who no longer needed his cybernetics, had them removed. After the removal process, he was still a man of formidable strength and speed, and possessed acute senses. Even when he re-received his emotions, only a small portion of his former self resurfaced and he was still regarded as a cold man by all, save for Manaroo.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

==Equipment==
===Armor===
Dengar's worn and faded body armor was a conglomeration of various Imperial armor components which served as an ever-present reminder of his Imperial past.<ref name="DB" /> The chest plate and undersuit were from a [[Cold assault stormtrooper|snowtrooper]], while the shoulder bells, gauntlets, midsection, codpiece, kneepads, and thighs were standard [[Desert stormtrooper/Legends|sandtrooper]] armor, which was a slight variant of [[Stormtrooper armor/Legends|stormtrooper armor]], with Dengar wearing two kneepads instead of the usual one. His facial wrappings, used in his younger days as a fashionable [[Turban/Legends|turban]],<ref name="CW4.20" /> later helped to cover and hide his cybernetic implants and scar tissue. During an assassination, he would often cover his mouth and nose, hiding his identity and adding to his intimidating demeanor.

===Weaponry===
[[File:Punishing_One_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Dengar disembarks from his ship, the [[Punishing One/Legends|''Punishing One'']]]]
Dengar carried with him an impressive array of weaponry. His weapon of choice was the [[Valken-38 blaster rifle/Legends|Valken-38 blaster rifle]], a [[Sniper rifle/Legends|sniper rifle]] that he used to kill or wound his prey from a long distance.<ref name="Card-SWGTCG-Valken-38 Blaster Rifle">{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|cardname=Valken-38 Blaster Rifle}}</ref> He also possessed one [[DL-21 blaster pistol/Legends|DL-21 blaster pistol]], [[DLT-19 heavy blaster rifle/Legends|DLT-19 heavy blaster rifle]], [[Concussion grenade/Legends|concussion grenades]], and a [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblade]].<ref name="DB" /> He was proficient, and in some cases overly enthusiastic, about using grenades and other explosives to complete a bounty.<ref name="Payback: The Tale of Dengar" />

===Vehicle===
Dengar's personal flagship was the ''Punishing One''. Initially a [[JumpMaster 5000/Legends|JumpMaster 5000]] scout ship, Dengar had it heavily modified with greatly improved sublight engines, and an array of weaponry including a mini-[[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]], [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedos]] and an [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2 unit]] controlled, quad-[[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannon]] system.<ref name="Gamer 7">''{{GamerCite|7|Harbingers of Doom}}''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The character's depiction in ''[[Payback: The Tale of Dengar]]'' by [[Dave Wolverton]] was inspired by the author's time as a prison security guard during college, capturing the air of "inner deadness" that incarcerated killers possessed.<ref name="dwolver">{{WebCite|url=http://boards.theforce.net/threads/lit-exclusive-dave-wolverton-addresses-fan-criticisms-of-the-courtship-of-princess-leia-more.50024454|text=Lit Exclusive: Dave Wolverton Addresses Fan Criticisms of The Courtship of Princess Leia, & MORE|archivedate=20151109053456}}</ref>

===Portrayal===
Dengar was played by British actor [[Morris Bush]] in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. He briefly appears in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], although it was unknown if it was still Bush in the role until Jeremy Bulloch confirmed it in the Celebration Europe II panel, The Fett-Tastic Four. He is played by voice-actor [[Joe Hacker]] in the audio adaption of ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]''. In the Star Wars series, his armor consists of bits of sandtrooper and snowtrooper armor, that were repainted from their original white. This was to point to his [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] past.<ref name="DB" /> [[Simon Pegg]] voiced Dengar in [[Bounty (episode)|''Bounty'']], an episode of the [[The Clone Wars: Season Four|fourth season]] of ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', which causes him to speak with a British accent.

In pre-production still photographs from [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], Dengar is pictured holding a modified WWII-era German [[Wikipedia:MG_34|MG 34]] machine gun (the basis for both the [[W-90 concussion rifle]] and [[DLT-19 heavy blaster rifle/Legends|BlasTech DLT-19]]). In the film, though, that weapon was held by bounty hunter droid [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]], and Dengar was armed with a modified German [[Wikipedia:MG_42|MG 42]] (as seen in the main profile image above).

===Other Appearances===
Dengar appears in the [[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|unabridged script]] of [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio drama]]. He has no lines, but Imperial Lieutenant [[Venka]] describes him as he stands aboard the ''Executor'' as a "former gladiator" with "twenty-three captures, six alive." The scene was cut from the [[New Allies, New Enemies|radio episode]], but the script was later published in book form.<ref name="ESB NPR">[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''The Empire Strikes Back'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref>

Dengar was slated to appear in the comic ''[[Jodo Kast & Dengar: Preying for Time]]'', a prequel series to ''[[Boba Fett: Twin Engines of Destruction]]'', however the comic was canceled.<ref name="Mangels">{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/jedicouncil/interview/mangels.shtml|text=TheForce.Net Cellblock 1138 - Andy Mangels Interview|archivedate=20011230041549}}</ref>

There is an easter egg in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' that features a rendition of the bounty hunter scene from Empire Strikes Back. Dengar is featured in this, along with all the other bounty hunters featured in the scene with Darth Vader.
